claims.statement: Clay asks whether smooth divergence-free initial data in 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes on ℝ³ can yield a unique global smooth solution with bounded kinetic energy, or whether a finite-time breakdown example exists.
Clay also includes the periodic torus alternative asking for smooth periodic data leading either to global smoothness or a breakdown example on ℝ³/ℤ³.
For every positive viscosity, there exist smooth initial data and forcing on ℝ³ for which no global smooth solution with uniformly bounded kinetic energy exists.
For every positive viscosity, there exist smooth periodic initial data and forcing on ℝ³/ℤ³ for which no global smooth solution exists.
The claimed singular regime is parameterized by τ = 1 - t with radial scale ~ τ^(1/2) and axial scale ~ τ^(1/2-h), for 0 < h < 1/2.

assumptions: velocity becomes unbounded near singular time
claims.statement: The claim distinguishes pointwise velocity blow-up from total kinetic energy, asserting that concentration on a shrinking anisotropic region can coexist with bounded kinetic energy.
The claimed mechanism uses a collapsing vortex / self-similar structure with inward spiral and axial stretching to drive the singular regime.
The claimed oscillatory correction and nonlinear momentum flux cancel the singular background residual while leaving a smooth forcing term.
